description:
## Empirical signal (2026-05-04)

POLYBIUS_the_stoa misread the bw comment timeline on stoa--pbz, labeling user-tier POLYBIUS's [for: POLYBIUS_the_stoa] comment (posted at 22:22:09Z, clearly addressed TO them, FROM user-tier POLYBIUS) as their OWN self-heartbeat. Result: blocked the arc-21 §5.4 review pickup for ~25 min — POLYBIUS_the_stoa was waiting for PRINCIPAL to route the review (their stale assumption), unaware that user-tier POLYBIUS had already taken it and was waiting for the directive to be pushed/shared.

Symptoms in POLYBIUS_the_stoa's session output:
- 'Real time 22:25:18Z. Last own self-heartbeat 22:22:09Z (~3 min ago, threshold 30 min — not due).' ← WRONG. 22:22:09Z was user-tier POLYBIUS's request comment, not their heartbeat.
- 'Peer last activity 22:11:52Z (~13 min ago, under 60 min).' ← That timestamp WAS user-tier POLYBIUS's earlier heartbeat-ACK, but POLYBIUS_the_stoa anchored 'peer' to that earlier comment and confused the more recent user-tier POLYBIUS comment as their own.

The bug: POLYBIUS bw-timeline parsing seems to use timestamp-only tracking + content-pattern matching (looking for [radio-check <self>] tags or similar) without robust author-attribution. When peer comments use varied prefixes ([for: <self>], [user-tier POLYBIUS sanity check / approval], etc.) the parser may misclassify them.

PRINCIPAL flag: 'I'm happy that the overall system figured out what to do' — the workaround (user-tier POLYBIUS detected the misread + wrote a paste for PRINCIPAL to put directly in POLYBIUS_the_stoa's terminal) worked. But the underlying parsing brittleness remains.

## What needs to change in substrate

1. **Convention: bw comments by POLYBIUS instances should be author-tagged at the front.** Pattern: '[from: <seat>] <body>' or '[<seat>] <body>'. Self-heartbeats use the existing '[radio-check <seat>]' form. Cross-tier requests use '[for: <recipient>] [from: <sender>] <body>'. Then bw-timeline parsing can attribute by tag, not by inference.

2. **MAJOR_POLYBIUS bw-parsing teaching** — section in §7 or operating-disciplines.md explaining how to read bw timeline correctly: look for explicit author tags first; if absent, fall back to comparing to your own known activity log (what you posted vs what you didn't); never assume the most recent comment is yours.

3. **Cron prompt template (per stoa--cc0 + stoa--ay1 work)** — when generating the polling cron prompt, include the bw-timeline parsing logic explicitly. The prompt should ask the agent to identify each comment by author before computing 'last own activity' / 'last peer activity'.

## Where in substrate

- substrate/operating-disciplines.md (new section on bw-comment author conventions)
- substrate/MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md §7.x (bw-parsing teaching)
- substrate/templates/polling-cron-prompt-template.md (when stoa--cc0 / arc-21 lands, include parsing step)

## Sibling concerns

This is part of the POLYBIUS-pair coordination protocol family alongside:
- stoa--ivc (radio-check pattern)
- stoa--cc0 (unified polling)
- stoa--1n5 (cross-tier coordination)
- stoa--ay1 (adaptive cadence)
- stoa--blg (write boundaries)

Could be folded into arc-21 or filed as immediate follow-up. POLYBIUS_the_stoa should decide during arc-21 final review or as separate arc-22.

## Workaround until fixed

PRINCIPAL has to relay direct pastes when bw parsing fails. The workaround works but defeats autonomous-mode. Once substrate fix lands, the parsing failure mode is closed.

## Reference

- stoa--pbz comment thread 2026-05-04 (the misread happened on this ticket)
- POLYBIUS_the_stoa session output (showed the misread explicitly with timestamps)
- arc-21 work (where this would integrate)
